title: Who is Tom Hart? Meet the man set to replace GP as Max Verstappen’s race engineer at Red Bull
extract: Tom Hart has been gradually taking over Max Verstappen’s race-engineering duties as Gianpiero Lambiase prepares to leave for McLaren. A mechanical engineer who joined Red Bull in 2012, Hart has worked with Verstappen since 2020 and took charge for the Las Vegas win.

title: OpenAI, Cisco launch ‘Shirudo’: How it protects Linux systems from security threats
extract: OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source eBPF-based tool that can apply temporary protections to live Linux systems while teams prepare permanent patches. Its safeguards can be tested before enforcement and use signed policies plus TPM-backed records.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
extract: Claude Ship adds agents for pull-request review, CI and merge-conflict fixes, and policy-based approvals. Anthropic recommends starting in observe-only mode and keeping human review for higher-risk changes as teams experiment with delegated code approval.

title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
extract: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s optimization technology and team to improve how AI models run on non-Nvidia chips, particularly its Trainium accelerators. The deal underlines how software optimization is becoming a strategic lever in the AI hardware race.

title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
extract: The UK’s NCSC says autonomous AI tools are accelerating intrusions by finding exposed systems, weak passwords and poorly secured developer APIs. The underlying weaknesses are often old security debt rather than novel vulnerabilities, making basic controls more important than ever.

title: Anthropic’s Alpöge says the 250,000-page Riemann proof figure was a joke
extract: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge clarified that the 250,000-page figure was a joke, not a proposed manuscript; the Lean code itself has been machine-checked, while the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as active rather than solved. Formal verification is not yet the same as broad mathematical acceptance.

title: Zstd 1.6 Released With Many Fixes, New Performance Optimizations
extract: Zstandard 1.6 brings faster decompression on AArch64, SVE2 compression optimizations and improvements for RISC-V vector extensions, alongside multithreaded and memory-safety fixes. It is a substantial update to a widely used open-source compression library.

title: Ladybird Web Browser/Engine Reaches Alpha
extract: The independent Ladybird browser and its from-scratch web engine have reached alpha after four years of development. Early builds are available for macOS and Linux, including Flatpak and distribution packages alongside source builds.

title: XNU Linux Lets macOS Userspace Processes Run On Linux
extract: XNU Linux runs Apple’s open-source XNU kernel as a loadable module inside an otherwise unmodified ARM64 Linux kernel, allowing macOS user-space processes to run alongside Linux processes without a hypervisor. The early demonstration boots a macOS 27 system disk to the desktop.

title: VKD3D 2.2 Released With More Improvements For Direct3D 12 On Vulkan
extract: VKD3D 2.2 advances Direct3D 12-on-Vulkan support for Wine, adding Shader Model 6.2 support, Vulkan shader float controls, HLSL handling improvements and compiler fixes. The release is expected to feed into the upcoming Wine 12.0 milestone.

title: Firefox 161 Brings Per-Site VPN Toggling, Classic Themes Section
extract: Firefox 161 adds per-site controls for its built-in VPN, a classic-themes section and developer-facing CSS improvements including the random() function and Typed OM changes. It is a useful feature release for both browser users and web developers.

title: LibreOffice 27.2 Alpha 1 Released For Testing
extract: The first LibreOffice 27.2 alpha adds JPEG-XL support, dynamic arrays in Calc, a new chart type and interface refinements ahead of the planned February release. The build is available for testing now.

title: Mesa 27.0 Merges LLVMpipe AVX-512 Support
extract: Mesa 27.0 has merged AVX-512 support for LLVMpipe, its software OpenGL driver. The work completes a long-running optimization effort, although the maintainer did not have modern AVX-512 hardware available for performance measurements.

title: Mesa 27.0 RadeonSI Gallium3D Disables Radeon Kernel Driver Support By Default
extract: Mesa 27.0 now disables compatibility with the legacy Radeon kernel driver by default for RadeonSI, steering early GCN 1.0 and 1.1 users toward AMDGPU and newer kernels. The compatibility switch remains available temporarily through AMD_DEBUG=use_radeon.

title: Mesa’s NVK NVIDIA Driver Another Step Closer To Vulkan Ray-Tracing
extract: Mesa’s open-source NVK driver has merged initial handling for Nvidia Tree Traversal Unit instructions, an important step toward Vulkan ray-tracing extensions on the open-source driver. Full ray-tracing support remains a longer-term goal.

title: CrowdStrike snaps up Zscaler in $44 billion deal as cyber threats mount
extract: CrowdStrike will acquire Zscaler in a $43.9bn all-stock transaction, a record cybersecurity deal that combines endpoint protection with secure application and data access. The companies expect the combined business to start with more than $10bn in annual recurring revenue.

title: The Blancpain Carrousel Incliné, a New Angle on Chronometric Precision
extract: Blancpain’s new 30-degree flying carrousel uses a sapphire case and dial to expose its calibre 222ISQ, with a 100-hour power reserve and a stated rate tolerance of 0 to +2 seconds per day. The movement’s inclined regulator is a technically ambitious development of the brand’s long-running carrousel work.

title: The Lebois & Co Heritage Atelier Chronograph Bleu-sur-Blanc, with Two-Tone Enamel Dial
extract: This limited-production chronograph pairs a grand feu two-tone enamel dial by Donzé Cadrans with a hand-wound La Joux-Perret LC-450 column-wheel movement. Its decimal scale divides each minute into 100 units, an unusual detail on a contemporary chronograph.

title: Just Because: Hunting for Vintage Watch Ads In A Brooklyn Basement
extract: Hodinkee follows collector Nick Federowicz through a Brooklyn archive of thousands of vintage magazines as he hunts for rare watch advertisements to sell as collectible art. The feature explores the visual history of brands including Rolex, Omega and Patek Philippe, and the people preserving their advertising ephemera.

title: More sex, different endings: how fan fiction makes our dreams come true
extract: The Guardian examines how fan fiction communities around worlds such as Harry Potter and Star Trek are influencing mainstream publishing, with popular online authors securing book deals. It is a lively look at the creative relationship between fandom, original fiction and commercial publishing.

title: Adder Stone by Clare Clark review – the story of a drowned Welsh village
extract: Clare Clark’s historical novel centres on a Welsh village drowned by a reservoir, using the submerged community’s history to explore memory, loss and place. The Guardian’s review highlights its blend of social history and haunting storytelling.

title: Battlestar Galactica’s Showrunner Loved One Scene The Sci-Fi Channel Wanted To Cut
extract: Ronald D. Moore recalls how the Sci-Fi Channel wanted a quiet Battlestar Galactica scene cut because it lacked action; he responded by making it longer. The anecdote reveals how deliberately the series protected its slower pacing and small human moments amid the war.

title: Gone Girl director David Fincher admits to lying about viral Ben Affleck Yankees hat story
extract: David Fincher has admitted that the famous story about a fight with Ben Affleck over wearing a Yankees cap in Gone Girl was invented to tease the actor. They did negotiate the hat, but the supposed multi-day production shutdown was Fincher’s joke.

title: The 13 biggest differences between The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping book and movie
extract: Entertainment Weekly compares the Sunrise on the Reaping film with Suzanne Collins’ novel, covering omitted scenes, toned-down violence, changed character arcs and the altered epilogue. It is a useful companion for readers of the book and fans of the adaptation.

title: Steven Spielberg to make a western written by Paul Thomas Anderson
extract: Steven Spielberg will direct The Heart in Winter, adapting Kevin Barry’s 2024 novel, with Paul Thomas Anderson writing the screenplay. Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance are set to star in the late-19th-century Western about two fugitives on the run.

title: AWS’s Strands Decider v2 targets agent decisions that hinge on a single detail
extract: AWS has released five open-weight Strands Decider v2 models built on Gemma 4, designed to score developer-supplied options rather than generate free-form text. The models read a whole scenario bidirectionally, can be fine-tuned and self-hosted, and are intended for routing, classification and policy decisions inside agent systems.

title: Meta’s Muse Personal AI Agent Launches in the UK
extract: Meta has brought Muse to UK adults, where the personal agent can work across connected apps and websites, including email, calendars, retailers and travel services. The rollout highlights its approval gates for sensitive actions, per-app permissions and isolated cloud computer.

title: Signal Now Blocks AI Screen Access to Protect Chats
extract: Signal is extending screenshot and screen-reading protections to iPhones and supported Android devices, preventing assistants such as Siri and Gemini from capturing private conversations. The controls are enabled by default on supported versions, addressing a gap that end-to-end encryption alone cannot close.

title: Google Search Gets Wallet Access, With Drive Coming Soon
extract: Google is adding an opt-in Google Wallet connection to Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode, allowing answers to draw on spending and card-rewards information. Drive and Gemini connections are planned next, while Wallet access is read-only and cannot move, manage or invest money.

title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
extract: Tidal will begin rejecting and removing wholly AI-generated tracks on December 9, after identifying more than 43% of recent uploads as AI-generated. AI-assisted music remains allowed; the move is a stronger response than the labelling approach used by larger services such as Spotify and YouTube Music.
